name: cross-graph diamond coalesce
topology: A in g1; B,C in g2 (reached from g1 via wire bridge); D in g1. Edges A→B, A→C, B→D, C→D — a diamond split across two single-threaded graphs.
input: A.down([[DATA, v]]) (one wave).
expect: DIRTY crosses the wire to B and C at the same priority as DATA (R12). Phase 1 DIRTY reaches D via both legs before any phase-2 DATA. D recomputes EXACTLY ONCE after both B and C settle in the same logical wave; D's outgoing wave contains a single DATA. No glitch (D never fires on a half-settled diamond).
note: L2.F mixed-locality survival proof — the diamond stays glitch-free even though B/C live in a different causal domain reached over the wire bridge.
blocked: wire bridge (backlog B2) — not yet implementable; the in-process diamond core it leans on is green in packages/ts core.test.ts (R-diamond/R-two-phase)

name: async-result arriving at paused node
topology: Producer P backed by an async (LocalAsync) pool → node N. N has one active pause lock.
input: 1) N.up([[PAUSE, L1]]). 2) P's async fn resolves while N is paused, delivering [[DATA, r]] toward N. 3) N.up([[RESUME, L1]]).
expect: The async result does NOT drop and does NOT deliver mid-pause; it enters N's pause buffer. On final-lock RESUME (L1 released, lockset empty) the buffered result replays as a wave to N's sinks. lock_id scope = the node-level pause_lockset (consistent with PAUSE buffering DATA).
note: DR-3 — async-result-at-paused-node is buffer+RESUME-replay, identical to how PAUSE buffers a synchronous DATA. Rust arm GREEN 2026-05-30 (CSP-6 Slice A): graphrefly-rs LocalAsync pool (dispatcher Vec<Pool> + register_async; invoke stays sync void, R-sync-core) + DeferredCtx (ctx.defer() owned late-emit, the Rust analogue of TS capturing ctx) + node pause_buffer. should_buffer_on_pause True-branch buffers an async COMPUTE node (deps>0); on_resume drains+replays [DIRTY,DATA]. Teeth-verified (disable the async-compute buffer → DATA delivers mid-pause). conformance.rs::c2_async_result_at_paused_node.

name: INVALIDATE × ctx.state × onInvalidate
topology: source S → derived D. D's fn sets ctx.state on each run and registers ctx.onInvalidate(flush). A second parent S2 → D exists (diamond) to exercise fan-in idempotency.
input: 1) S settles [[DATA, v]] → D runs, caches, sets ctx.state. 2) S.down([[INVALIDATE]]) — cascades to D via both fan-in paths in one wave.
expect: D broadcasts INVALIDATE downstream exactly ONCE (not once per fan-in path). D's onInvalidate hook fires exactly once (external flush). ctx.state is NOT wiped — INVALIDATE is lifecycle-continue, not a fresh-lifecycle transition; any internal reset must be done manually in onInvalidate. D's per-dep prevData returns to SENTINEL so a downstream prevData===SENTINEL never-emitted detector reads correctly. A second INVALIDATE arrival in the same wave is a no-op (hook + broadcast do not re-fire).
note: distinguishes lifecycle-continue (INVALIDATE) from fresh-lifecycle wipe (deactivation / resubscribable reset). TS arm covers single-parent cascade + idempotent no-op + state-preservation; fan-in-in-one-wave needs batch (covered by R-invalidate-idempotent _hasData guard). Rust arm GREEN 2026-05-29 (CSP-5 control/terminal slice): graphrefly-rs node.rs INVALIDATE branch (idempotent !has_data guard, dep_prev→SENTINEL, dirty un-wedge) + ctx.on_invalidate (re-callable, cleared on deactivate); conformance.rs::c3 covers single-parent cascade + idempotent no-op + state-preservation, matching the TS arm (diamond fan-in-in-one-wave still needs batch, deferred).

name: mixed sync/async diamond
topology: A → B (sync LocalSync leg) and A → C (async LocalAsync pool leg); B→D, C→D. One diamond, one sync leg + one remote/async leg.
input: A.down([[DATA, v]]).
expect: D joins EXACTLY ONCE after BOTH legs settle, even though the async leg C settles later via a pool callback. The async pool callback's wave-state mutation serializes back onto the graph's single thread (R-graph-domain), so D's dirty-dep accounting reconciles the sync and async settlements into one recompute. The first-run gate holds D until both deps have delivered real DATA. R-dirty-before-data: a post-activation re-join emits DIRTY before DATA in the same logical wave (observed ['DIRTY','DATA'], glitch-free two-phase).
note: R8/R9 PoC validated; TS arm now a full conformance test (sync + async pool, same process — no wire bridge needed). R-dirty-before-data earned here via the post-activation re-join DIRTY-before-DATA assertion (CSP-3, 2026-05-28). Rust arm GREEN 2026-05-30 (CSP-6 Slice A): the async leg is a derived_async node whose fn stashes ctx.defer() and emits later; the first-run gate holds the join until it delivers, and the async leg's no-emit run is EXEMPT from the undirty-RESOLVED synthesis (deferred ≠ rejected — else the join settles early). Teeth-verified (remove the async exemption → the join fires before the async leg settles, runs=2 not 1). conformance.rs::c4_mixed_sync_async_diamond.

name: PAUSE lockset multi-source
topology: node N with two independent pause controllers, A and B.
input: 1) A.up([[PAUSE, LA]]). 2) B.up([[PAUSE, LB]]). 3) A.up([[PAUSE, LA]]) again (duplicate). 4) A.up([[RESUME, LA]]). 5) B.up([[RESUME, LX]]) for an unknown LX. 6) B.up([[RESUME, LB]]).
expect: After step 1-2 lockset = {LA, LB}, N paused. Step 3 (same-id repeat PAUSE) is idempotent — lockset unchanged. Step 4 removes LA; lockset = {LB}; N STILL paused (B's lock holds). Step 5 (unknown id) is a no-op. Step 6 removes LB; lockset empty; N truly resumes (fires once with latest dep values under default mode). Releasing one controller never resumes the node while another's lock is held.
note: multi-pauser correctness by construction — paused state derives from lockset.size > 0. Rust arm GREEN 2026-05-29 (CSP-5): graphrefly-rs node.rs pause_lockset (HashSet) + up() PAUSE/RESUME (same-id idempotent, unknown-RESUME no-op) + default-mode coalesce (maybe_run skip-while-paused → on_resume fire-once-with-latest); conformance.rs::c5. The resumeAll/false modes + async-paused buffering = C-9/C-10 (deferred to the async pool).

name: synchronous feedback cycle → ERROR
topology: state S → derived D=([S], n=>n+1) → effect E=([D]); E's fn synchronously calls S.set(...) (a write back to S, an indirect dep of E), so S→D→E plus the feedback write closes a cycle.
input: Kick the graph so E's fn runs and synchronously re-drives S (S.set) before E's wave completes.
expect: The re-entrant attempt to run E's fn while E is already mid-wave is detected node-locally (E's in-wave flag is set) and rejected: a node ON the cycle emits [[ERROR, e]] (the graph layer catches the substrate throw at the value-level wrapper nearest the throw on the synchronous unwind — D30; which node is implementation-determined, e.g. D or E), and the wave aborts deterministically. NO silent _pending desync, NO unbounded synchronous recursion / stack overflow, NO surviving half-settled state. A legitimate accumulator over the same S built with ctx.state (scan) does NOT trigger the cycle (no topological re-entry).
note: B10 / D37. Separates a disguised imperative control-flow loop (rejected) from ctx.state accumulation (allowed). Detection reuses the existing _insideRunWave flag (zero new structure); error ownership graph-level (D30); dispatcher uninvolved. Async feedback across a turn boundary (async pool) is a separate, out-of-scope case. Rust arm GREEN 2026-05-29 (CSP-5): Rust has no graph layer yet, so the D30 catch is a catch_unwind at the substrate WAVE-OWNER (the outermost subscribe/down/up/set entry). A panic = the Rust analogue of a value-level throw (the fn signature is Fn(&Ctx)->(); R-reentrancy mandates unwind, not graceful return); it converts to [[ERROR,e]] on the blamed cycle node (the innermost fn that ran = the effect E). Whole-cascade wave-flag recovery via the thread-local WaveScope touched-set closes B25 (conformance.rs::c6 also asserts the post-error source re-emits its leading DIRTY — teeth-verified by disabling the emitted_dirty reset). Per-language impl (D24, like the AnyValue value-rep decision) — no spec-amend / no D#.

name: upstream control at a depless source
topology: depless source S (cached value) → derived D → sink. D (or a sink on D) originates ctx.up([msg]) which forwards upstream to the terminus S.
input: Three independent runs, one per upstream-allowed non-pause control kind: 1) D.up([[INVALIDATE]]). 2) D.up([[DIRTY]]). 3) D.up([[TEARDOWN]]).
expect: INVALIDATE: S HONORS the invalidate-request — S.cache returns to SENTINEL, S's onInvalidate hook fires once, and S broadcasts INVALIDATE downstream so D (and the whole downstream cone) clears (D.cache → SENTINEL, D's onInvalidate fires). DIRTY: DROPPED at S — S unchanged (cache + status intact), NO downstream DIRTY, downstream is NOT left wedged awaiting a settle. TEARDOWN: DROPPED at S — S not terminated, NO downstream TEARDOWN. A node guard on S may deny the INVALIDATE (drops silently) — opt-out, not the default.
note: B11 / D38. Closes the F-NO-IMPL-DEFINED gap on upstream control reaching a depless source. INVALIDATE-up is a cache-drop request (not an imperative write); DIRTY/TEARDOWN have no coherent terminus action. Dep-bearing intermediates forward only; source is the single actor, down-cascade the effect. Formal: wave_up_source.tla. Rust arm GREEN 2026-05-30 (CSP-6): Core::up — PAUSE/RESUME self-handle the lockset; otherwise a depless source (deps empty) is the terminus (INVALIDATE → self.down([INVALIDATE]) honor, DIRTY/TEARDOWN drop) and a dep-bearing intermediate forwards toward each dep (dup_control reconstructs the payload-free kind, Msg not Clone). Teeth-verified (disable the terminus INVALIDATE → S keeps its cache). conformance.rs::c7_upstream_control_at_depless_source.

name: intra-graph runtime rewire
topology: sources A, B (B carries a cached DATA b0); derived D = ([A], fn) — D initially depends only on A. All in one graph (D22 single causal domain).
input: 1) A settles [[DATA,a1]] → D's first-run gate opens, cache=fn(a1). 2) D.subscribeDep(B, fn2). 3) B settles [[DATA,b1]]. 4) D.unsubscribeDep(A, fn3). 5) A settles [[DATA,a2]]. 6) D.replaceDeps([B], fn3) (current set, idempotent). Variants: remove A while A's DIRTY is mid-flight to D; A sends [[INVALIDATE]] then D.unsubscribeDep(A); A goes terminal then attempt D.subscribeDep(A) / attempt a rewire on a terminal D / subscribeDep(self) / a cycle / mid-fn rewire.
expect: Surgical (Option-C): a rewire touches only changed deps — kept deps keep their subscription + DepRecord, no unsub/resub. (2) subscribeDep(B) with B cached → B's cached value reaches D via the subscribe handshake (START then [DATA,b0] per R-push-subscribe) and D recomputes; the first-run gate is NOT re-armed (D already passed it — it does not re-wait for a fresh round of all deps); an added SENTINEL dep delivers START only, no recompute until it emits. (3) B's update drives D. (4) unsubscribeDep(A) discards A's DepRecord + clears A's dirty contribution; if A was the sole dirty contributor and D was dirty, D AUTO-SETTLES; D's cache is PRESERVED across every rewire (R-rom-ram). (5) after unsubscribeDep(A) a2 NO LONGER drives D — A's edge is DRAINED so no stale DIRTY/DATA/INVALIDATE strands. (6) replaceDeps to the current set is idempotent (no spurious recompute, no DepRecord churn). A mid-wave removal (A's DIRTY in flight) auto-settles per above; a removed dep's queued INVALIDATE is drained, never lands. REJECTS (throw → graph-layer ERROR, not silent): self-dependency; a cycle; replaceDeps/subscribeDep/unsubscribeDep on a terminal D (completed/errored); adding a non-resubscribable terminal dep (resubscribable terminal allowed); mid-fn rewire (a fn mutating its own topology mid-wave = the D37 feedback-cycle ERROR) and reentrant rewire. unsubscribeDep to zero deps → degenerate fn-no-deps, cache preserved, no auto-deactivate. Every rewire requires an explicit fn (positional fn-deps pairing). INTRA-graph only (D22); no cross-graph rewire form.
note: D42/CSP-2.5; R-rewire (since D22, refined by D42). SUBSTRATE prerequisite for higher-order operators (mergeMap/switchMap/concatMap/exhaustMap/flatMap). Formal (SD-2 gate, all four cross-axes): wave_rewire.tla = per-node Q1–Q7 + rewire×INVALIDATE (NoStaleEdgeMessages) + rewire×terminal (RewireOnlyOnLiveNode), TLC-green 603k states; wave_rewire_emit.tla = rewire×equals (CacheMatchesLastData) + rewire×multi-sink (MultiSinkConsistent), TLC-green 3003 states; all four new invariants mutation-verified load-bearing. TS arm GREEN 2026-05-28 (landed as setDeps/addDep/removeDep in @graphrefly/ts node.ts; renamed by D115 to replaceDeps/subscribeDep/unsubscribeDep; conformance.test.ts C-8 + rewire.test.ts 12 unit tests); rust/py arms pending CSP-5/CSP-7. R-rewire FLIPPED ACTIVE 2026-05-28 (TS-arm-green+formal precedent). Rust arm GREEN 2026-05-30 (CSP-6): graphrefly-rs node.rs landed set_deps/add_dep/remove_dep on Node<T> + Core::rewire; renamed by D115 to replace_deps/subscribe_dep/unsubscribe_dep — surgical Option-C via per-dep CURRENT-index boxes (Rc<Cell<i64>>: kept-dep reorder = O(1) box reroute, removed dep box→-1 drain), fn-swap re-register + B32 unregister-old (slotmap GC, freeing the rewired-away closure), push-on-subscribe for an added cached dep, atomic multi-add settle (in_dep_mutation defers maybe_run → ONE two-phase DIRTY→DATA via settle_rewire), Q6 unsubscribe_dep auto-settle (+ zero-dep un-dirty RESOLVED), first-run gate + cache preserved (Q2/Q7). Rejects panic-propagate externally (self-dep/cycle-DFS/terminal-self/terminal-dep/reentrant); a MID-FN rewire becomes [[ERROR,e]] via the wave-owner catch (R-reentrancy/D37, Rust substrate bundles the D30 catch). conformance.rs::c8 (surgical + terminal-reject) + node.rs 11 rewire unit tests; teeth-verified (disable box-reroute → reorder fails; disable atomic defer → fires on a partial SENTINEL view). rust uses the existing TLA+ (wave_rewire.tla + wave_rewire_emit.tla, SD-2 already met). py:todo (CSP-7).

name: pausable:false async source ignores PAUSE (keeps producing)
topology: depless async-pool source S with pausable:false (timer/interval-class) -> sink.
input: 1) subscribe a sink to S. 2) S.up([[PAUSE, L1]]). 3) S's async fn resolves, emitting [[DATA, r]] while the lock is held.
expect: DATA is delivered to the sink IMMEDIATELY (DIRTY+DATA), NOT buffered -- pausable:false ignores PAUSE/RESUME entirely; the lockset is never consulted and production continues through the PAUSE (contrast C-2, where a pausable compute node buffers). A subsequent RESUME is a no-op (nothing buffered).
note: D44 -- pausable mode is the outer gate over R-async-paused; false dominates (resolves B20). Rust arm GREEN 2026-05-30 (CSP-6 Slice A): Node::producer_opts(pool:Async, pausable:False); should_buffer_on_pause returns false for Pausable::False, so the leaf source's deferred production delivers immediately ([DIRTY,DATA]) under a held lock. conformance.rs::c9_pausable_false_async_source_ignores_pause.

name: true-mode async leaf source delivers own production immediately under PAUSE
topology: depless async-pool LEAF source S, pausable:true (default; fromPromise/fromAsyncIter-class) -> sink.
input: 1) subscribe a sink to S. 2) S.up([[PAUSE, L1]]). 3) S's async fn resolves, emitting [[DATA, r]] while the lock is held.
expect: DATA is delivered to the sink IMMEDIATELY (DIRTY+DATA), NOT buffered -- in true mode PAUSE gates recomputation/propagation, not a leaf source's OWN production ('production-gating is resumeAll's job'). A COMPUTE node (deps>0) in the same position WOULD buffer (C-2); with pausable:'resumeAll' the leaf source WOULD buffer.
note: D44 -- the true-mode leaf-source carve-out extends to async production (B20's twin). Rust arm GREEN 2026-05-30 (CSP-6 Slice A): Node::producer_async (pausable:true default); the should_buffer_on_pause True-branch requires deps>0, so a depless async LEAF source delivers its own production immediately under PAUSE (the deps.is_empty() leaf-vs-compute discriminator). conformance.rs::c10_true_mode_async_leaf_source_delivers_immediately.

name: higher-order inner rewire at the wave boundary
topology: outer source S; operator OP = ([S], fn) in one graph (D22). fn: on S DATA v -> inner = makeInner(v); ctx.rewireNext.subscribeDep(inner, fn). on an inner COMPLETE -> ctx.rewireNext.unsubscribeDep(that inner, fn). switch-variant: on S DATA -> ctx.rewireNext.unsubscribeDep(prevInner, fn) + ctx.rewireNext.subscribeDep(newInner, fn). Inners are leaf sources whose deactivation is observable (a flag set in onDeactivation).
input: 1) S [[DATA,v1]] -> OP requests subscribeDep(innerA). 2) wave settles -> drain -> innerA added+subscribed, cached DATA pushed [DIRTY,DATA]. 3) innerA DATA -> forwarded. 4) (switch) S [[DATA,v2]] -> OP requests unsubscribeDep(innerA)+subscribeDep(innerB). 5) drain -> innerA unsubscribed+drained, loses last subscriber -> _deactivate -> onDeactivation fires (cancellation observable); innerB added. 6) (merge) two inners live -> both forward. 7) an inner COMPLETEs -> unsubscribeDep -> drain removes it (bounding). Variants: IMMEDIATE in-fn this.subscribeDep (not via rewireNext) -> REJECTED (D37); rewireNext then OP terminal same wave -> queue still drains after terminal; no-net-change rewireNext -> no-op.
expect: A rewireNext NEVER mutates _deps while _insideRunWave is true (deferred to the post-settle drain). The drain runs at the COMMITTED boundary (after batch commit / final-lock RESUME, never on an un-committed/paused view). Each queued op applied exactly once, in deterministic order (per-node FIFO, causal node order), as a fresh wave. Added cached dep pushes [DIRTY,DATA]; first-run gate NOT re-armed. Removed dep DRAINED (no stale DIRTY/DATA/INVALIDATE strands) and, if last subscriber, _deactivates + fires onDeactivation = observable input-side teardown (switchMap cancel/abortInFlight; mergeMap bounding). switch: only the current inner forwarded AND the superseded inner's source torn down (not merely masked). IMMEDIATE in-fn self-rewire still throws -> graph-layer ERROR (D37). Terminal OP still drains pending rewireNext requests at the boundary: unsubscribeDep releases the auxiliary dep (observable deactivation), subscribeDep/replaceDeps may change topology, and any later dep messages are absorbed by the terminal output guard (no downstream post-terminal DATA/RESOLVED/INVALIDATE/COMPLETE/ERROR). No-net-change rewireNext = no-op (no boundary-drain loop). INTRA-graph only.
note: D47/R-rewire-deferred, amended by D62. Distinct from C-8 (external/immediate rewire between waves): C-11 is SELF-triggered/deferred-at-boundary. D62 revises the prior terminal facet: a node going terminal no longer discards already-queued rewireNext requests; the queue drains at the committed boundary, while terminal remains an output/lifecycle guard. Formal: wave_rewire_deferred.tla TLC-green after D62 (41,137 generated / 15,367 distinct / depth 24) with five invariants: DeferredAppliedAtBoundary, DrainExactlyOnce, RemovedDepSilenced, NoBoundaryDrainLoop, NoPostTerminalOutput. Runtime arms were reset because the previous TS/Rust passes implemented/tested terminal-discard. Required implementation update: remove the terminal-discard guard from deferred rewire application; add terminal-drain tests proving (a) queued unsubscribeDep after terminal deactivates/releases the helper dep, (b) queued subscribeDep/replaceDeps after terminal may change deps, and (c) later dep messages produce no downstream post-terminal output. Batch/pause deferred-drain timing and rollback fate are split into C-25 / R-rewire-deferred-committed-boundary (B24 + D110). Rust arm GREEN 2026-05-31: D62 catch-up -- queued ctx.rewire_next drains even if the owner becomes terminal in the same wave; terminal remains an output guard (no post-terminal DATA/RESOLVED/INVALIDATE/COMPLETE/ERROR). conformance.rs::c11 updated from terminal-discard to terminal-drains-topology.

name: occurrences stay DATA; RESOLVED is undirty-only (no equals-substitution)
topology: (a) a source emitting a repeated value (fromIter([1,1,1])-class) -> sink. (b) the same source -> take(3) -> sink. (c) source -> filter(pred rejecting every value) -> downstream node -> sink. (d) source -> distinctUntilChanged -> sink. All intra-graph (D22).
input: (a) source emits 1,1,1 then COMPLETE. (b) same into take(3). (c) source emits values all failing the filter pred (each a dirty+settle round). (d) source emits 1,1,2.
expect: (a) the sink observes THREE DATA (1,1,1) then COMPLETE -- a repeated value is a distinct occurrence, NEVER collapsed to RESOLVED (no equals-substitution). (b) take(3) emits [1,1,1] then COMPLETE (counts occurrences, not distinct values). (c) the filter, DIRTY'd but rejecting (no tier-3 value), has the substrate SYNTHESIZE one undirty RESOLVED per wave to clear the downstream dirty -- no DATA, no wedge; RESOLVED here means dirtied-but-no-value, never value-unchanged. (d) distinctUntilChanged (opt-in dedup, its own eq) emits [1,2] -- dedup is the OPERATOR's job, not the substrate's. Every node settle is >=1 DATA XOR 1 RESOLVED, never mixed. NodeOptions.equals does not exist.
note: D49/R-resolved-undirty supersedes D15/R-equals. Pins the un-overloaded RESOLVED (undirty-only, substrate-synthesized) + no substrate dedup. Formal: wave_protocol.tla equals-substitution axis removed (+ retire wave_protocol_custom_equals_MC / wave_protocol_equals_false_MC); wave_rewire_emit.tla equals axis revised. RUST ARM GREEN 2026-05-30 (CSP-6): the D49 behavior already landed in the substrate (CSP-5 /qa); conformance.rs::c12 expresses take/distinctUntilChanged as inline ctx.state derived nodes (no operator library yet — per-language D6/D24): (a) a producer emitting [1,1,1]->3 DATA (no equals-substitution); (b) take(3)->[1,1,1] (occurrences, not distinct values); (c) filter-reject->one substrate-synthesized undirty RESOLVED per wave, no wedge; (d) distinctUntilChanged opt-in dedup->[1,2] with the deduped repeat an undirty RESOLVED. rust:pass. py:todo (CSP-7).

name: INVALIDATE arriving at a paused compute node
topology: compute node N = ([D1,D2], fn) paused via its own lockset (default/'true' mode); D1, D2 are sources. fn guards SENTINEL deps (reads prevData/data, emits only when present).
input: Three runs. (a) SOLE-DEP CANCEL: N has run once; PAUSE N; D1 settles [[DATA,v1]] (buffered, N does not recompute); D1 sends [[INVALIDATE]]; RESUME N. (b) RE-ARM: PAUSE N; D1 [[DATA,v1]]; D1 [[INVALIDATE]]; D1 [[DATA,v2]]; RESUME N. (c) MULTI-DEP SURVIVE: PAUSE N; D1 [[DATA,v1]]; D2 [[DATA,v2]]; D1 [[INVALIDATE]]; RESUME N.
expect: (a) the INVALIDATE PROPAGATES downstream immediately while paused (N broadcasts INVALIDATE, cache→SENTINEL, onInvalidate fires); on RESUME N does NOT recompute (the paused dep-wave was superseded — N is SENTINEL, nothing to recompute) — NO spurious undirty RESOLVED, and crucially NO recompute against a SENTINEL dep (so a non-guarding fn does NOT panic→spurious terminal ERROR). (b) on RESUME N recomputes ONCE with D1=v2 (the post-INVALIDATE DATA re-armed the buffer; v1 was superseded). (c) on RESUME N recomputes ONCE with D2=v2 and D1=SENTINEL (the fn guards D1) — the D1 INVALIDATE did not cancel the recompute D2's buffered change warrants (no lost update). In all cases the downstream dirty bookkeeping stays balanced (N's leading DIRTY is cleared by either the INVALIDATE or the resume settle).
note: D50 / R-paused-invalidate. The INVALIDATE×PAUSE analogue of D44/C-9/C-10 (async×PAUSE). Surfaced by the CSP-5 Rust /qa (finding A): the impl left paused_dep_wave_occurred set after an INVALIDATE → resume recompute against a SENTINEL dep → spurious ERROR (Rust) / garbage value (TS). Formal: wave_paused_invalidate.tla (ChangedImpliesLive + PendingReflectsChanges + NoAllSentinelRecompute), TLC-green 327 states + ChangedImpliesLive mutation-verified. BOTH ARMS GREEN 2026-05-29: TS (node.ts INVALIDATE branch + conformance.test.ts C-13 a/b/c) + Rust (node.rs receive_from_dep INVALIDATE branch attributed-cancellation + conformance.rs::c13) — both impl-fixes teeth-verified (disable the cancellation → C-13(a) fails: superseded wave recomputes). R-paused-invalidate flipped active. py:todo (CSP-7).

name: cleanup hooks are per-run (cleared + re-registered each fn run)
topology: source S → derived D. D's fn registers BOTH ctx.onInvalidate(flush++) and ctx.onDeactivation(cleanup++) on EVERY run, then emits.
input: 1) S settles [[DATA,v1]] → D runs (registers run-1 hooks). 2) S [[DATA,v2]] → D re-runs. 3) S [[DATA,v3]] → D re-runs (D has now run 3×). 4) S.down([[INVALIDATE]]). 5) unsubscribe D's last sink (D deactivates).
expect: After 3 runs, the INVALIDATE (step 4) fires onInvalidate EXACTLY ONCE (the current/run-3 registration), NOT 3× — the prior runs' onInvalidate registrations were cleared at each run-start and discarded without firing (D28 onRerun-cut). Deactivation (step 5) fires onDeactivation EXACTLY ONCE (run-3's), NOT 3×. A single-run node keeps its one registration (no re-run → no clear). Both hooks behave uniformly (clear-and-re-register).
note: R-cleanup-hooks per-run lifecycle (D28 clarification, no new D#). Surfaced by the CSP-5 Rust /qa (finding E, parity-consistent): push-only hook lists fired K stale hooks after K runs. Fix = clear BOTH hook lists before each fn invocation (run_wave/_runWave), re-register from the fn body. No TLA+ (cleanup hooks are a registration-list lifecycle, not in the wave_protocol formal state model). User-approved uniform clear-and-re-register + no-new-D# 2026-05-29. name: a dep's terminal releases its in-wave DIRTY contribution (no wedge)

name: an absorbed-error dep counts as TERMINAL for auto-COMPLETE (no wedge, order-independent)
topology: join node D = ([B, C], fn) with completeWhenDepsComplete:true (default) AND errorWhenDepsError:false (ABSORBS a dep error, like a rescue/catch); B and C are independent sources. A control node Dctrl = ([B, C], fn) with the DEFAULTS (errorWhenDepsError:true) to show the non-absorbed contrast.
input: (a) error-then-complete: C emits [[ERROR,e]] (D absorbs it — errorWhenDepsError:false, D stays live), THEN B emits [[DATA,b],[COMPLETE]]. (b) complete-then-error (reverse order, the load-bearing order): B emits [[DATA,b],[COMPLETE]] FIRST (D not yet all-terminal — C live), THEN C emits [[ERROR,e]] (absorbed, terminating LAST). (c) contrast: Dctrl over the same C-errors — with errorWhenDepsError:true the dep ERROR auto-cascades to ERROR (the absorbed path is NOT taken; the complete-check never runs).

(b) SAME result regardless of order: when C's absorbed ERROR lands LAST, the ERROR-absorbed receive-arm MUST mirror the COMPLETE arm's `completeWhenDepsComplete && all-deps-terminal -> COMPLETE` check and emit COMPLETE — NOT route silently to settle leaving D live forever (the wedge B42 fixes). With the OLD 'all deps Complete' logic D never completes in EITHER order (C's terminal=Error != Complete blocks _allDepsComplete forever). (c) Dctrl auto-ERRORs on C's error (errorWhenDepsError:true fires before any complete-check) — confirms the absorbed path is gated on errorWhenDepsError:false.

name: raw ctx waveData is the only dep-value input and terminal metadata is lightweight
topology: sources A and B feed raw ctx node N. N records the raw ctx shape it observes and uses ctx.waveData to decide whether to emit. A dynamicNode variant declares A+B but conditionally reads only A.
input: (a) no-wave: B changes in a way that does not deliver any wave projection to A's slot for this invocation. (b) resolved: a dep dirties then settles with a RESOLVED-only wave. (c) data+invalidate same wave: a dep emits [[DATA,1],[DATA,2],[INVALIDATE]] in one upstream msgs array. (d) null data: a dep emits DATA null. (e) empty-array data: a dep emits DATA with payload []. (f) terminal dirty-clear: a dep emits COMPLETE, and another variant emits ERROR with a valid diagnostic payload; explicit ERROR false/true are rejected by R-data-payload, while binding/source adapters coerce host-language boolean failures before emitting ERROR. (g) dynamic unread: B delivers a fresh wave while the fn chooses not to read/propagate B.
expect: Raw ctx exposes `waveData` as the sole dep-value input field; it does not expose `latest`, `prevData`, `latestData`, `depRecords[i].latest`, or an equivalent parallel value alias. For each dep i, `waveData[i]` is a list of per-wave projections for THIS invocation. No delivered wave is `[]`; a RESOLVED-only wave is `[[]]`; `[[DATA,1],[DATA,2],[INVALIDATE]]` projects as `[[1,2,SENTINEL]]`; DATA null projects as `[[null]]`; DATA [] projects as `[[[]]]`; two waves DATA null then DATA [] project as `[[null],[[]]]`. INVALIDATE uses the protocol SENTINEL marker (TS undefined / Rust-Py sentinel equivalent), which cannot collide with DATA because DATA(SENTINEL) is rejected by R-data-payload. COMPLETE/ERROR do not enter waveData; `ctx.terminal[i]` is false for no terminal, true for COMPLETE, or the legal non-boolean ERROR payload for ERROR. A helper such as track/current/latest, if present, is derived and must not change the raw ctx value shape. The dynamicNode variant can inspect `waveData[i]` to early-return on an unread-dep-only wave, producing only the substrate undirty RESOLVED, while a read dep DATA propagates normally.
note: D77+D78. This conformance scenario replaces the ambiguous `depRecords.latest`/`prevData`/`batch` raw ctx wording with one canonical two-dimensional waveData contract: dep -> waves -> values/settle markers, plus separate lightweight terminal metadata. It is a ctx input-shape scenario, not a new message tier or wave-ordering rule. Formal: wave_ctx_wave_data.tla pins the distinguishability of no-wave vs RESOLVED vs DATA(null) vs DATA([]) vs DATA+INVALIDATE, the absence of a second modeled latest/prevData value source, and the terminal distinction between none/COMPLETE/ERROR payload. D78 also pins that ERROR false/true are invalid payloads, preserving the false/true terminal shorthand. name: snapshot restore preserves graph state and rejects local-only factories
topology: Original graph G contains a named restorable node N with a cached DATA value, node-private ctx.state, and a live topology edge visible in describe(); it also contains an anonymous/local-only node L. A fresh target graph G2 has the same factory registry for N but no code body for L. A second variant removes N's factory from the registry.
input: 1) Run G so N has cache value v and ctx.state s, including non-persist state. 2) Take a graph snapshot/checkpoint. 3) Hydrate/restore G2 from that checkpoint: storage/decode work is modeled as async/bootstrap work outside the sync core; the resolved checkpoint commits at a graph boundary. 4) After ready/commit, subscribe to N in G2 and inspect describe/profile-visible topology. 5) Attempt cross-process restore of L and attempt restore with N's factory missing. 6) Incremental restore/diff variant: apply a persisted change after the baseline restore.
expect: The restored named node N has the checkpointed cache/value absence, ctx.state s (including non-persist state), and live topology/factory identity; restore did NOT perform a fresh-lifecycle wipe, did NOT reset cache to SENTINEL, did NOT re-arm N as never-run, and did NOT fire fresh cleanup hooks merely because the graph restored. A late subscriber after ready receives N's restored cached value directly through normal push-on-subscribe; restored dependency activation/push-on-subscribe does not by itself recompute, overwrite, or clear N's restored cache. Ordinary upstream DATA/INVALIDATE/terminal events after the restore commit may update N normally. The graph is not externally ready during async hydration; no partial restored state leaks before the restore commit. The restore commit is graph-boundary ordered: if applied to a live graph or via incremental diff replay, externally visible changes pass through the normal batch/wave/observe path rather than hidden mutation. The local-only anonymous node L is honestly marked non-cross-process-restorable and fails restore; a missing factory reference also fails restore. Storage tiers, WAL frame bytes, codecs, and content-addressed envelopes are not asserted by this scenario.

It also pins D25's factory-name model and D82's separation between graph restore semantics and storage binding/WAL details.
